literal: If hair is lost, not living yak-beast like those, life will give up, if honor [threatened] comes.
translation: Those who value their honor like the yak, which does not survive if it loses its hair, will give up their lives if their self-respect is threatened.
modern: தன் உடம்பிலிருந்து மயிர் நீங்கினால் உயிர் வாழாத கவரிமானைப் போன்றவர்கள், தங்களுக்கு மானக் குறைவு வரும்போது உயிரை விட்டுவிடுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet compares highly self-respecting individuals to the 'kavarimā' (yak), a beast traditionally believed to die of grief if it loses its hair. The word 'māṉam' here represents personal honor, dignity, and self-respect. The phrase 'uyir nīppar' shows that for such noble people, physical existence is worthless if their honor is compromised. The poet emphasizes that preserving one's integrity is far more valuable than preserving one's physical life.
